target_customer: Benefits consultants and brokers, insurance carriers and employers (originally employees through their employers)
problem: Employees overspend on and underuse health and voluntary benefits, and benefits teams drown in manual document and data work. Pasito started on the employee side and now sells AI agents to the benefits industry.
business_model: B2B SaaS sold to brokers, carriers and employers
product_category: AI benefits and insurance workflow software

founders.name: Pauline Roteta
founders.background_notes: YC page: senior investor and portfolio manager at BlackRock, CFA charterholder, Certified Financial Planner, Fulbright Scholar.

technical_complexity.rationale: Employee facing benefits navigation needed data integration with payroll and plan documents. The later AI document ingestion product is harder, but in 2022 it was mostly standard engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Plan and census data integrations create some lock in once deployed, but benefits navigation was a crowded space with several funded rivals.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No evidence that incumbents copied or bought it. Aggregators list Nayya and Benefitfocus as alternatives, with no dates.

market_need_then: Employers spend heavily on benefits and employees often pick poorly. The 2022 launch pitched savings on healthcare and payroll costs for both sides.

branding.domain_note: Site at pasito.ai; an older profile references joinpasito.com. History not sourced.

identity.voice_and_tone: Positions as the AI native workspace for benefits.

brand_strength.rationale: No press on the brand itself. The name is shared with an unrelated Barcelona baby goods brand, Pasito a Pasito, which can confuse search.

pivots.from: Employee facing benefits navigation and decision support
pivots.to: AI agents for carriers, brokers and benefits vendors
pivots.why: Reason not stated. The 2022 launch targeted employees, the current site targets consultants, carriers and employers.

outcome_analysis: Pasito raised a $3.25M seed in October 2022 after YC, then repositioned toward AI agents for benefits brokers and carriers. In February 2026 it raised a $21M Series A led by Insight Partners. The company claims thousands of employers use it and names large brokers as customers. The shift to selling to the benefits industry plus the AI timing appears to have unlocked the larger round, though those usage figures are self reported.
notes: Seed reported by Coverager and a press release republished October 25, 2022 (search listing; Coverager page was blocked). Total raised conflicts across aggregators ($24.4M, $42M). A FF News profile names Julie Scotland as co-founder and the YC launch post mentions a Julie, but neither was opened as a company source, so she is not listed as a founder. Competitor list empty because only undated aggregator lists exist.
